original.target_description: Experiment 1 contraction bias: multiple candidate regressions in supplied primary manuscript; requested target correspondence unresolved.

notes: Identity: canonical title Visual biases in judging body weight and all four named authors match ref_o. The supplied text is a full primary research manuscript (30 numbered pages, methods, results, references and figure legends), with blinded recruitment affiliations; no DOI, journal/year imprint or explicit version date is printed, so exact published-version identity is not independently established. No PDF was supplied. The locator p.5 cannot be mapped securely to this manuscript pagination; manuscript p.5 is introductory material. Study 1 and the broad description do not select weight versus BMI regression, intercept versus slope, or pilot versus main analysis. Main-data candidates on manuscript pp.9–10: estimated weight on actual weight, β0 = 19.60 (t = 11.99, p < .0001), β1 = 0.71 (t = 26.96, p < .0001); estimated BMI on actual BMI, β0 = 5.39 (t = 7.01, p < .0001), β1 = 0.79 (t = 23.51, p < .0001). These are printed regression parameters; their standardisation is not explicitly labelled. The distinct tests of slope against 1 are F(1,118) = 124.18 and F(1,118) = 36.93, respectively, both p < .0001; these are not the coefficient t tests. Pilot p.9 reports mean beta 0.77 across five participants, separately from main data. Candidate main-model analytic N = 120 image-level observations: p.7 explicitly identifies 120 stimulus photographs, p.9 regresses mean estimated weight for each image, and Figure 1 p.28 explicitly states one point per image. This is not derived from df. The 29 women recruited for the full experiment contribute judgments, not 29 independent observations in that image-mean regression; five pilot participants are separate, and 22 is a power-planned count. Recruitment excludes current/history of eating disorders; no image-level analytic exclusions are stated. Because target coefficient correspondence remains unresolved, 120 is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review. No N sum or effect-size conversion performed. Only n_o and es_value_o are assigned; replication, p and success are unassigned placeholders.
